A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Misleading ChartQA benchmark and Region-Aware Misleader Reasoning (RAMR) pipeline. Their main texts, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison. The changed evaluation sampling requires caution when comparing scores.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 16 MLLMs under baseline, zero-shot CoT, and RAMR settings, together with performance breakdowns and failure analysis.

after.justification: v4 reports updated and additional model evaluations, performance breakdowns, failure analysis, and quantitative outcomes from expert validation of generated questions.

M1.justification: The augmentation/refinement workflow and RAMR procedure remain substantively unchanged: localize misleading regions, overlay bounding boxes, and answer using original and annotated charts. Matched prompts in v1 Appendix A.7 and v4 Appendix A.11 retain the same instructions. Expanded seed-selection and validation descriptions do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 3,026 MCQs spanning 21 misleaders, 10 chart types, and 60 misleader–chart pairings. Revised appendix examples and newly disclosed seed counts remain within this coverage. The changed evaluation fraction concerns sampling rather than additional tasks or domains.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPT-4.1, GPT-o3, GPT-o4-mini, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Gemini-2.5-Flash, and InternVL3-8B/38B/78B-MPO, while removing InternVL2.5-1B/2B-MPO. This substantially revises the evaluated comparator set. v4 actually tabulates 22 models despite claiming 24.

E3.justification: v1 Section 3.1 specifies a balanced random sample of 20%, or 605 cases. v4 Section 2.4 designates 30% as a higher-quality testing set, while Appendix A.6 reports randomly sampling approximately 30%. This materially revises the reported evaluation sample; exact membership and whether retained results were rerun are not established. Metrics and prompting conditions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The misleader and chart-type analyses are retained. v4 Section 4.3 revises failure analysis around GPT-o1 and InternVL3-78B-MPO, adding question misunderstanding to localization and interpretation errors. Section 2.4 also adds a quantitative audit of rejected, revised, and approved generated samples. No new controlled ablation or robustness experiment is reported.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its model evaluations. The human-performance standard deviation is attributed to prior work in both versions. Added model averages and validation percentages are descriptive results rather than new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial model results and aggregate rows, revises existing scores, and updates misleader/chart breakdowns. For example, DeepSeek-VL2-Small's reported CoT accuracy changes from 31.96% to 21.24%. The newly evaluated InternVL3-78B-MPO reports 51.94% pipeline accuracy, versus v1's best reported 48.77% for InternVL2.5-78B-MPO. Changed sampling and model membership prevent interpreting these as equivalent-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The conceptual misleader taxonomy is retained. Neither version introduces mathematical theorems, proofs, formal assumptions, or substantive derivations; the expanded methodological explanations do not add formal theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the stated evaluation contribution from 16 to 24 MLLMs, although Table 1 supports 22. The central contributions remain the benchmark, its taxonomy, evidence of difficulty with misleading charts, and the RAMR pipeline.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations for CoT regressions in reasoning models, distinguishes corrective reasoning from question misunderstanding, and argues that controlled augmentation limits bias or knowledge leakage. Its distribution caption also explains uneven chart frequencies. Existing interpretations of visual versus data reasoning and the zero-shot/no-fine-tuning limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v4 documents 155 seed MCQs, including 122 selected and 33 newly authored questions, the three-of-four expert selection rule, and validation of 4,263 generated samples. It adds the labeling interface, detailed review guidelines, and multiple-expert confirmation requirements. The anonymous sample-dataset link is replaced with a named GitHub dataset link. These substantially expand documented reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v4 adds Tonglet et al. (2025) and model references such as the Qwen2.5-VL and DeepSeek-VL2 reports. The positioning against small human-oriented misleading-chart evaluations remains substantially unchanged. Most detailed related work is retained in Appendix A.1 rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: The introduction and benchmark-construction narrative are extensively rewritten and expanded. The explicit research-question structure is removed, diagnostic analyses move into Discussion and Error Analysis, implementation details move to the appendix, and the main related-work section becomes a summary of an appended full review.

P2.justification: The construction and RAMR diagrams are redrawn, result tables gain reorganized groups, averages, and highlighting, and the chart-performance plot is restyled. v4 adds a labeling-tool screenshot and revises or replaces appendix MCQ figures, including questions and answer labels. Prompt templates are extensively reformatted from full-width boxes into two columns.

improvement.justification: The seed provenance and explicit expert-review protocol in v4 Sections 2.2–2.4 and Appendices A.4–A.5 make the benchmark substantially easier to scrutinize, while the expanded failure analysis improves its diagnostic value. These gains are tempered by inconsistent model counts, an imprecisely specified revised test sample, and the claim of consistent pipeline superiority despite counterexamples in Table 1. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
